method: Behaviour cloning from four single-skill experts

observation.invariant: each expert's native observation is a prefix of this layout, so experts are driven by slicing and no adapter can drift; pinned by tests/test_opendoge_skills.py

architecture.actor: rsl_rl MLPModel, 512-256-128 ELU, empirical observation normalization, Gaussian with scalar std
architecture.why_flat: Per-skill output heads and a zero-initialised per-skill residual were both implemented and measured; both are worse on handover (see rejected), so the flat shared output layer ships.
implemented_but_not_shipped: src/tasks/multiskill/rl.py: SkillHeadedActor (one independent head per skill)
src/tasks/multiskill/rl.py: SharedResidualActor (shared head + zero-init per-skill residual)

expert_selection.criterion: Kept the pair that measured best on handover. The jump expert is the retrained moving jump (5000 iterations, full budget: one target-height flight per cycle 1.00, four-feet contact agreement 0.98, takeoff stagger median 1 control step, velocity error 0.067 m/s), which is why this baseline differs from the previous in-place-jump one.

reference_protocol.note: GPU rollouts are not bit-reproducible: repeated runs at a fixed seed differ (measured: transition aggregate sd ~0.002, handstand->walk range 0.66-0.74). On CPU repeated runs were bit-identical, so the source is the Warp/GPU solver. Compare challengers on means of repeated runs at seeds 0/1/2 with these exact commands, never on a single run.
reference_protocol.observation_noise: same commands with --corruption (the actor's training-time observation noise)
reference_protocol.train_config: same transition command with --train-config (interval pushes and episode resets)

robustness.observation_noise_per_skill_seed0: walk 1.000 / 0.074, handstand 0.972, getup 0.978, jump peak 0.086 m / recovery 1.000
robustness.note: the baseline holds its transitions both under observation noise and under the full training condition (pushes + resets).

reference_metrics.jump_criteria_note: The old 0.070-0.080 m peak band belonged to the in-place jump task and was re-derived for the moving jump: the unified environment has no push event, so the shipped number is the push-free peak (0.0828 m over 3 seeds). The standalone task's higher 0.146 m peak is inflated by the push_robot event it retains in its play config.

sota_adoption_rule: Run the reference protocol at seeds 0, 1 and 2 and repeat each run (GPU rollouts vary at a fixed seed); compare means, never single runs.

Reject if any per-skill metric is worse than the reference by more than the measured run-to-run plus seed spread: walk velocity error > 0.068 (reference mean 0.0589 plus ~2 sd; the previous 0.06 cap sat below the walk expert's own 0.059 fidelity inside the unified environment and was unsatisfiable by construction), handstand < 0.95, getup < 0.93, jump substantial flights per cycle outside 0.9-1.1, jump four-feet contact agreement < 0.95, jump recovery < 0.96, jump peak outside 0.075-0.090 m.

Replace only if the transition aggregate improves beyond the measured run-to-run spread (>= 0.945 against the 0.9355 reference), or the weakest cell handstand->walk rises above 0.70 while the aggregate holds above 0.93.
A better single-seed or single-run aggregate is not sufficient: run-to-run spread alone reached 0.002 on the aggregate and 0.08 on handstand->walk.

rejected.per-skill output heads (SkillHeadedActor: 3 seeds: transition aggregate 0.9255 and handstand->walk 0.491 against the flat head's 0.9389 / 0.678, with identical per-skill metrics. Root cause: the cloning data contains no handover frames, so independent heads have nothing from which to learn the handover, while a flat head interpolates one continuous function across skills.
rejected.per-skill heads + handover data: collecting real skill switches (opendoge-collect --handovers, ~1.1M frames labelled by the target expert) recovered only part of the gap: aggregate 0.9301, handstand->walk 0.552. Still below the flat head.
rejected.shared head + zero-init per-skill residu: 0.9288 / 0.555. Zero initialisation fixes the starting point, not the end point: the residuals grew over 30 epochs and landed where the independent heads did. Penalising residual magnitude, rather than re-initialising, is what would be needed.
rejected.PPO fine-tune LR 5e-5: 900 iterations; transitions 0.865, walk velocity error 0.054 -> 0.296, handstand -11 points
rejected.single-seed walk-interference claim: retracted: the 0.008 m/s gap attributed to the jump data is smaller than the same policy's seed spread (0.0141).

selection: Single policy covering walk / handstand / get-up / jump with a 57-field observation. Re-registered after two changes that made the previous artifact unable to run at all: the observation gained the jump's 3-field twist block (54 -> 57), and the jump task was redesigned from an in-place jump into a moving one with one target-height flight per cycle (expert retrained at full budget). All four datasets were re-collected in the new layout and the student was re-cloned. Reference metrics, the observation-noise condition, the full-training condition and the run-to-run spread were all measured before registration (docs/opendoge_multiskill.md sections 5.5, 5.7 and 5.8).
